claims.explanation: Isoxsuprine's selective cytotoxicity is likely driven by its dual activity as an ADRB2 agonist and CDK1 inhibitor. Sensitive lines are enriched for activating RTK/PI3K pathway mutations (EGFR, PIK3CA, MET, KIT, MAP2K1) and cell-cycle checkpoint loss (TP53, CDKN2A), which increase dependence on CDK1 for mitosis. Resistant lines frequently have PTEN loss or chromatin-remodeling mutations (KMT2D, CTNNB1) that may provide survival buffering.
